name: Senior / independent living
summary: Age-restricted, service-enriched rental (or entry-fee) apartments with central dining, commercial kitchen, wellness, activity and transportation spaces; usually 3-5 story wood or podium buildings, sometimes with cottages. Per-SF cost is close to podium multifamily but the large common-area share (~30-40%) raises gross SF per unit. Per-SF data come from Weitz's national senior-living cost survey (2025-26); per-unit figures are derived via gross SF per unit.

typicalSize.method: Typical stand-alone IL community 100-200 units; campus IL buildings larger (judgment).

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Gross SF per unit: IL apartments average ~850-1,050 net SF (vs Census median new rental 1,000 SF, e5) and common areas (dining, kitchen, wellness, lounges, corridors) take 30-40% of gross => ~1,200-1,450.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Suburban 3-4 story IL ~25-40 units/acre; urban podium IL higher (judgment from multifamily densities).

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: IL residents own fewer cars than general-market renters; zoning commonly 0.75-1.0 per unit plus staff (judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived: perSF x sfPerPrimaryUnit: mid $270 x 1,300 = ~$350k; low $225 x 1,100 = ~$250k; high $360 x 1,450 = ~$520-530k.

perSF.method: Weitz 2026 mid-level IL $240-292/SF (midpoint $266) and high-level $283-362 (e1), essentially unchanged from the April 2025 brief ($239-290 / $282-361, e2). Mid $270 = mid-level midpoint + a small on-site allowance; low $225 = below mid-level for value suburban product; high $360 = top of the high-level range.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. general conditions, OH&P, commercial kitchen equipment, on-site work; excludes land, soft costs, FF&E, off-sites, impact fees, financing, pre-opening/marketing. Weitz does not state whether its ranges include sitework - verify.

qualityTiers.method: Weitz high-level vs mid-level IL midpoints: $322.5 / $266 = 1.21 (e1) sets premium; luxury (entry-fee CCRC-grade) and economy (age-restricted, light services) by judgment.

systemSplit.method: Derived from the podium split in this category: +2.5 pts equipment (11, commercial kitchen/servery, laundry), +1.0 pt HVAC (23, dining/kitchen exhaust, more conditioned common area), +0.5 pt elevators (14), +0.4 pt each low-voltage (27, emergency call) and fire alarm (28); offset by -2.0 pts concrete (03, less podium parking), -0.5 framing, -1.0 site; 01 absorbs rounding.

lineItems.name: Commercial kitchen, servery and dining equipment

cost.method: Derived: full-service restaurant-style kitchen and bistro equipment, hoods, walk-ins (2026 judgment).
Derived: wireless pendant/pull-cord call system with locating (2026 judgment).

lineItems.name: IL cottages / villas (per SF of cottage)
lineItems.notes: Optional - set qty to the cottage SF planned.

lineItems.name: Under-building parking (per SF of parking area)
lineItems.notes: Optional - roughly 350 SF of parking area per space.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived: dining room, bistro, lounges, theater, fitness/wellness, library and outdoor furniture plus smallwares ~ $1.2-2.7M for 150 units (2026 judgment); IL units are unfurnished.

pctOfHard.method: Derived: RAND multifamily soft/hard 0.19-0.33 incl. financing (e6) plus senior-specific design/consulting and pre-opening; mid 0.25 excluding construction interest and operating pre-opening/marketing (model separately). | Second pass (2026-10-24, main session): Reduced 4 points: RAND-based, includes developer costs. The engine adds impact & tap fees, the developer fee and construction financing as their own lines (docs/BUDGET_ENGINE.md §5), so this bucket must exclude them.

softCosts.notes: Add pre-opening, marketing/lease-up and operating deficit reserves separately - lease-up of IL is slow (often 18-30 months).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard low $250k x 1.12 ~= $280k; hard high $530k x 1.45 ~= $770k.

source.title: Assisted Living Construction Costs Rise in 2026, Independent Living Costs Remain Flat (Feb 3, 2026; Weitz 'Senior Living Construction Costs' report)

evidence.quote: Table 3.1 Panel C. Soft Costs: Texas Market rate $22; Colorado Market rate $44; California Market rate $84 (vs Panel A hard costs $115 / $237 / $253 per NRSF)
evidence.scopeNotes: Soft/hard ratios derived: TX 0.19, CO 0.19, CA 0.33. RAND soft costs include A&E, legal, fees and financing costs; market-rate sample mixes garden, podium, wrap, high-rise.

openQuestions: Weitz per-SF scope (sitework, FF&E) not stated in the public summaries; the full report would confirm.
No public per-unit IL project budgets (e.g., state CON filings, HUD 231 or tax-exempt bond offering documents) were captured - the per-unit mid is derived via SF per unit.
Common-area ratio varies 25-45% by service level; it moves per-unit cost more than per-SF cost.
